column1: # T_TEST.7 pt.1 — known findings, each with the reason it is known.
# Format (ZAP baseline `-c`):  <ruleId>\tIGNORE|WARN|FAIL\t<comment>
# Columns are separated by a single TAB. Lines starting with `#` are comments.
# The rule for this file: a line exists only when somebody can say why the
# finding does not apply here. "Noisy" is not a reason on its own — a rule that
# fires on every page and is silenced without a sentence is how a real finding
# gets hidden six months later. Anything not listed stays at ZAP's default, and
# the pass/fail decision itself lives in `app/cli/zap_report.py`, not here:
# exit codes spread across a TSV and a shell script are a gate nobody can read.
# Timestamp Disclosure — matches any 10-digit number in a response. Our bundles
# are minified JS full of hashes and ids, and the SPA sends `expires_at` /
# `verified_at` on purpose (D-EVIDENCE-DECAYS: a date is *required* next to a
# claim). Every hit so far is one of those two.

column3: Dates are deliberate (D-EVIDENCE-DECAYS); the rest are bundle hashes.

column1: # Suspicious Comments — fires on `TODO`, `FIXME`, `admin` etc. inside vendored
# minified JS. Our own comments do not ship: the production build strips them
# (T_SEC.2, static bundle), so what remains is third-party source text.

column3: Hits are inside vendored minified JS; our comments are stripped at build.

column1: # Modern Web Application — informational, and correct: this is a React SPA.
# It reports that links are rendered by script, not that anything is wrong.

column3: Informational: yes, it is an SPA.

column1: # Non-Storable Content — informational. API responses are deliberately
# non-storable; that is the intended answer for authenticated JSON.

column3: Informational; non-storable is the intent for authenticated JSON.

column1: # Sec-Fetch-* headers not set — these are request headers set by browsers, not
# something the server can emit. Fires because ZAP's own spider does not send
# them.

column3: Request-side headers; the scanner not sending them is not a server defect.

column1: # --- deliberately NOT ignored, listed so nobody adds them later without ---
# --- reading this: ---
# 10035 HSTS, 10038 CSP, 10020 X-Frame-Options, 10021 X-Content-Type-Options,
# 10063 Permissions-Policy — all five are set by nginx (T_SEC.1, D-DOCS-EXPOSURE).
# If any of them fires, the header stopped being sent. That is a real regression
# and must not be silenced here.
